https://baltic-review.com/poland-ai-heal.text: Share Tweet 0 A University of Warsaw initiative is bringing technical and healthcare experts together to discuss responsible uses of artificial intelligence. A Polish academic initiative is continuing its summer programme on artificial intelligence in healthcare with a free online webinar on Wednesday, August 5. The series, organised through the Interdisciplinary Centre for Mathematical and Computational Modelling at the University of Warsaw, is designed to connect technical knowledge with the practical, legal and organisational questions surrounding medical AI. The programme is being delivered in cooperation with MCSC Hospital Leadership Innovation as part of the wider Gaia AI Factory consortium. According to the University of Warsaw centre, the sessions are intended for healthcare professionals, researchers, technology companies, start-ups and others interested in the use of artificial intelligence in medicine. A broader view of medical AI Rather than presenting artificial intelligence as a single tool or product, the series approaches the subject from several directions. The organisers say speakers will discuss technological possibilities, business considerations, regulation, legal responsibilities and experience from the implementation of new solutions. That interdisciplinary structure is important for a field in which the technical performance of an algorithm is only one part of the practical question. Healthcare organisations must also consider how systems are introduced into existing workflows, how data are handled, who remains responsible for decisions and how professionals can assess the limitations of automated tools. The University of Warsaw’s event page lists the August 5 meeting as one of several webinars scheduled between July and September 2026. Earlier sessions took place on July 8 and July 22, while additional meetings are planned for August 19 and September 2. Each webinar is expected to last approximately one hour and conclude with a question-and-answer session. Part of Poland’s expanding AI infrastructure The webinar series is linked to Gaia AI Factory, a European Union-funded project in which the University of Warsaw’s computing centre is involved. The project page describes Gaia AI Factory as a Polish facility intended to provide infrastructure and services for the development and deployment of advanced artificial-intelligence applications. The project is coordinated by ACC Cyfronet at AGH University of Science and Technology in Kraków and supported by a national consortium of research and technology institutions. The University of Warsaw’s role includes participation in a wider ecosystem connecting research, industry and public-sector users. According to the project description, the planned infrastructure will include a high-performance computing system with approximately 1,000 graphics-processing units divided between training and inference tasks. The platform is intended to support the full development cycle, from preparing data and training models to validation, deployment and monitoring. The project also places emphasis on human skills. Its activities are expected to include workshops, hackathons, online courses and mentoring, with the aim of strengthening national competence in artificial intelligence. Healthcare is identified as one of the project’s strategic areas, alongside space-related applications and public administration. Why the discussion matters For hospitals and other healthcare providers, the introduction of AI is not limited to purchasing software. It can involve data governance, staff training, procurement, legal compliance, evaluation of results and long-term monitoring. A forum that brings together researchers, practitioners and technology specialists can help make those questions visible before systems are adopted at scale. The series also reflects a shift in how universities contribute to technology debates. Academic centres are not only developing computational methods; they are increasingly acting as meeting places where technical research can be tested against professional experience and public responsibilities. Participation in the webinars is free, although advance registration is required. The University of Warsaw says detailed information about individual sessions is announced through the MCSC platform and the Gaia AI Factory profile. The August 5 session therefore offers a timely snapshot of Poland’s effort to build both the infrastructure and the expertise needed for responsible artificial intelligence. Its focus is practical rather than promotional: how emerging tools may be assessed, adapted and governed in one of the most data-sensitive areas of public life. https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/mi.text: A BMW driver took police on a 'dangerous' chase before his passenger's body was pulled from flood water. Polish national Adrian Osiecki was behind the wheel of a BMW X5 towing a caravan when it was pursued by officers. The caravan was eventually unclipped from the BMW, which was then driven off 'at speed' before plunging into water and hurtling into a wall. Osiecki, 34, ran from the scene and was later arrested, while his passenger's body was discovered in the water. Despite medical treatment, he could not be saved and was pronounced dead. READ MORE: Walsall van driver, 50, gets three points on his licence for doing 57mph on motorway Following his arrest, Osiecki provided a short statement to officers in which he denied driving the car and said he had not stolen the caravan. Osiecki, of Friars Road, Coventry , later admitted handling stolen goods, dangerous driving, driving while disqualified, driving without insurance and drug-driving. He was jailed for 16 months and handed a two-year driving ban at Derby Crown Court on Tuesday, September 15. Derbyshire Police said the vehicle was pursued following reports it had been stolen from Oakerthorpe, Derbyshire, in the early hours of Saturday, February 14. Osiecki was seen to carry out a 'number of dangerous manoeuvrers', putting the safety of officers and members of the public 'at risk'. The force said: "This included ramming police cars, swaying the caravan into the path of pursuing vehicles and driving in the middle of the road in an attempt to obstruct officers from stopping the vehicle. "At one point the caravan is unclipped from the vehicle before the car is driven off at speed before going into a large amount of standing water and crashing into a wall on a bridge in Main Street, Egginton." Osiecki ran towards fields before he was arrested a short time later. The force went on: "A second man who had also been inside the vehicle left the scene and entered the flooded Egginton Brook. "After extensive searches by police and Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service over several hours, the 40-year-old Polish man was recovered from the water. "He was treated by ambulance crews at the scene and taken to hospital, where he was pronounced dead." READ MORE: Secret to getting the best of BirminghamLive's stories Detective Inspector Simon English said: "This was a highly dangerous pursuit during which the offender put the safety of our officers and that of the public at considerable risk by carrying out a number of dangerous manoeuvres. "We are pleased that the case has been resolved at court and Osiecki will be spending time behind bars, where he should seriously consider the consequences of his actions. "We will continue to target those who drive on our roads in a dangerous manner and I hope the sentence given at court sends a clear message that dangerous offending of this kind will never be tolerated." Derbyshire Constabulary said it referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) as the 'man's death happened after police contact'. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cwe8r2.text: 'It's really hard to believe' - How Oregon primary school shooting unfolded 'It's really hard to believe' - How Oregon primary school shooting unfolded Close Four victims, including a teacher and three children aged 5, 8 and 11, were killed in a shooting at a primary school in the US state of Oregon, local police say. A 16-year-old suspect forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors. He was also killed in the shooting by an armed member of the community who followed the suspect inside the school, police said at a press conference. Two additional victims, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were hurt and transported to hospital in critical condition. https://www.g4media.ro/trei-explicatii-d.text: Funcționăm ca organizație non-profit, iar banii rezultați din contribuțiile cititorilor sunt destinați integral finanțării proiectului G4Media. G4Media a primit, marți, trei explicații diferite de la AUR despre venirea AfD în București: Reprezentanții partidului neonazist din Germania au fost la protest, nu au fost invitați dar probabil vor veni sau participă, de fapt, la alt eveniment din Parlament, din ”festivalul libertății de exprimare”, așa cum a numit George Simion seria de 150 de evenimente, conform AUR, întinse pe mai multe zile. George Simion, Petrișor Peiu și Mihail Neamțu au avut variante diferite despre venirea și invitațiile adresate AfD, a cărei șefă Alice Weidel a atacat românii din Germania, pentru protestul despre care autoritățile susțin că se anunță a fi violent. Deputatul AUR Mihail Neamțu a declarat, duminică , pentru G4Media, că la protest au primit invitații și reprezentanții AfD, dar acestea au fost trimise înainte de ”declarațiile controversate ale doamnei Alice Weidel”. Întrebat dacă după declarațiile lui Weidel (care a condamnat românii pentru că ”jefuiesc sistemul de asistență socială” din Germania) i-a transmis acesteia că fie își retractează declarațiile, fie îi retrage invitația, Mihail Neamțu a declarat că celor de la AfD li s-a comunicat viziunea AUR, dar nu a răspuns concret dacă i-a retras invitația. George Simion a negat, însă, într-o declarație pentru Gândul tot de duminică faptul că reprezentanții AfD vor participa la protest, dar nu a exclus posibilitatea ca aceștia să participe la manifestație: Liderul AUR a precizat, în aceeași zi, că la manifestația din Parcul Izvor au fost invitați reprezentanți ai unui partid din Polonia, apropiat președintelui Karol Nawrocki. Ulterior, într-un interviu difuzat luni , tot la Gândul, Simion a spus că o să-i invite la protest pe membrii AfD ca observatori, ca să observe mișcările stradale și să internaționalizeze evenimentul, și nu să se implice în protest. Nu în cele din urmă, Petrișor Peiu a declarat, luni, la B1 TV, că nu vede ce ar avea să caute membrii AfD la protestul lui Călin Georgescu de sâmbătă subliniind că aceștia vor veni, dar vor participa la evenimentele din weekend, cu referire la ”festivalul libertății de exprimare” așa cum l-a numit Simion. Întrebat de G4Media la ce evenimente va participa AfD Petrișor Peiu a răspuns că nu se ocupă de acest eveniment, dar și că nu a declarat acest lucru. Confruntat cu emisiunea, Peiu a declarat că este vorba de mai multe conferințe și nu este implicat în organizarea lor, deci nu are detalii. explicatia e ca AUR se …. pe votantii lor Ce definiție mai bună pentru AUR=Trădători de neam si slugi ale Rusiei dacă ei sunt prieteni cu Afd care ponegresc românii? AFD se pisă pe românii din diaspora iar AUR aplaudă !!! In traducere haurista: rublele „e slabe” pe piata valutara,dar daca „e foarte multe te scoate din saracie”. Simioane, abia acum ai o problema. Le prezinti lupul oilor ce te-au votat! Misto!
